title: Catching game build card
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Variables in games and e-bullying
source: Seeded from computing/y6 lesson 7 (Catching game build card (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 7: A catching game: selection and score. To understand how selection checks a condition to change a variable in a game

questions.q: Build the falling script on the Apple.
questions.a: go to top, forever change y by -5.
questions.model: Teacher builds the start position and the forever loop, then runs it.

questions.q: Add the if touching Bowl block inside the loop.
questions.a: if touching Bowl? then change score by 1, go to top.

questions.q: Add arrow-key scripts to the Bowl.
questions.a: right: change x by 20; left: change x by -20.

questions.q: Core: Finish the catching game and test it 5 times. Write the scores.
questions.a: A working game; five test scores recorded.
questions.model: Teacher plays once and talks through what to watch for.

questions.q: Extend: Add a second 'if': if y position < -170 then change lives by -1 and go to the top.
questions.a: A miss below the bowl loses a life.

questions.q: Stretch: Make the apple fall faster as score goes up. Which block do you change?
questions.a: Use change y by (-5 - score / 2), or a 'speed' variable.

questions.q: 'if touching Bowl? then' is... A) a loop B) selection C) an event
Why must the if block be inside the forever loop?
questions.a: So the condition is checked again and again as the apple falls.
